To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the MRs from two basal ray-fined fish, Amur sturgeon Acipenser schrenckii and tropical gar Atractosteus spatula, are activated by a broad range of steroids including Prog and aldosterone, but with different potencies than the human MR.
Prog is a potent agonist of fish MRs and that Prog signaling in fish may not be a useful model for human Prog signaling.

(1) the EC50s of sturgeon and gar mineralocorticoid (MR) are between 8 and10 pM and 13 and 15 pM, respectively; (2) the MR from zebrafish, a teleost, has an EC50 of 75 pM and (3) human MR has an EC50 between 65 and 200 pM.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolution of steroid hormone receptors, in particular the evolution of MRs.
the evolution and function of MRs in fish and humans.
the physiological regulation of fish by corticosteroids, including Prog, and the evolution of the MR.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Prog and its derivatives are agonists for MRs in all vertebrates, but the mechanism of action of Prog and its analogues as MR agonists is different in ray-finned fish compared with mammals.
MRs in sturgeon and tropical fish are more similar to each other than to human MR.
Prog is an MR agonist in zebrafishes and in other fish.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Prog, spiro, and 19nopro act as MR agonists, not antagonists, in sturgeon, gar and zebrafishes.
MRs from Amur sturgeons and tropical gars, as well as zebrafish, are more similar than they are to human MRs in terms of steroid sensitivity.
the MRs of these two basal ray-finned fishes are similar to each other and to the zebrafish but different from human MR in their responses to steroids.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the MRs of sturgeon and gar, which diverged from human MR ∼450 million years ago, have retained the ability of human MR to bind and respond to Prog, which is a major steroid in fish and is hypothesized to have evolved in early vertebrate ancestors.
MRs from two basal ray-fanned fishes are responsive to low concentrations of corticosteroids and progesterone and that the Prog response is not mediated via serine-810.
MRs from two basal actinopterygian fishes are highly responsive to corticosterone and aldosterone and that Prog and spironolactones can act as agonists for these fish receptors.
